svg.aria-label: Questions that narrow the choice of method. Predict or explain: To explain, choose a model whose parts can be read: regression coefficients, or a short tree. Quantity, count or yes/no: Quantity: linear or polynomial regression. Count: Poisson or negative binomial. Yes/no: logistic. Beyond the sampled range: Neighbours and tree models stay level past the data. A regression model follows its shape, right or wrong. Hundreds or thousands: A few hundred noisy examples suit a simple curve. Many thousands give the flexible methods room. Who must accept it: People can check a short tree or a regression model; hundreds of trees need extra tools to explain. A note says: when unsure, fit a regression model and a forest; if the forest wins by a lot, the regression model is missing a shape.
svg.text: Questions that narrow the choice
THE AIM
Predict or explain
To explain, choose a model whose parts can be read:
regression coefficients, or a short tree.
THE OUTCOME
Quantity, count or yes/no
Quantity: linear or polynomial regression. Count:
Poisson or negative binomial. Yes/no: logistic.
THE RANGE
Beyond the sampled range
Neighbours and tree models stay level past the data.
A regression model follows its shape, right or wrong.
THE DATA
Hundreds or thousands
A few hundred noisy examples suit a simple curve.
Many thousands give the flexible methods room.
THE AUDIENCE
Who must accept it
People can check a short tree or a regression model;
hundreds of trees need extra tools to explain.
When unsure, fit a regression model and a forest. If the forest wins by a lot,
the regression model is missing a shape.
